summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (CentOS Stream 10, Erlang 26 via RabbitMQ's official packagecloud el/9 repos since el/10 packages don't exist yet), created the `payments` vhost with an `app_user` account (full configure/write/read permissions on that vhost), and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all three nodes. Verified messages published to the queue survive the loss of any single node and remain consumable from the surviving nodes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for all three nodes via `systemctl reboot`, confirming changed boot_id and full service/data/cluster recovery each time while maintaining quorum.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 3 nodes: CentOS Stream 10, no RabbitMQ/Erlang pre-installed
Installed EPEL and RabbitMQ's official packagecloud Erlang and Server RPM repos on all nodes; rewrote el/10 baseurls to el/9 since RabbitMQ has no el10 build yet
Installed erlang-26.2.5.4 and rabbitmq-server-3.13.7 on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts and set up cluster SSH keypair for inter-node scp
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and copied it (verified matching md5sum) to node2/node3 with rabbitmq:rabbitmq 0400 ownership
Opened firewalld ports 4369/25672/5672/15672 on all nodes (was silently blocking join_cluster with erpc noconnection errors)
Enabled/started rabbitmq-server on all nodes; joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3/3 disk+running nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin; created payments vhost, app_user account, and full permissions on payments via rabbitmqctl
Installed python3-pika on all nodes to exercise real AMQP publish/consume as app_user
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' (x-queue-type=quorum, initial group size 3) in payments vhost; confirmed members=[node1,node2,node3]
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded ack); confirmed boot_id changed and all 5 previously published durable messages survived and were consumable afterward
Published 5 fresh messages, restarted node2 via systemctl reboot; confirmed boot_id changed and cluster/queue recovered

Published 5 more messages, then stopped node3 (rabbitmqctl stop_app) confirming via node1 cluster_status that node3 was down, and consumed all 10 pending durable messages from node2 while node3 was down, proving survival/consumability with one node lost; restarted node3's app and confirmed 3/3 nodes running again
Rebooted node3 via systemctl reboot as final mandatory restart; confirmed boot_id changed and full cluster/vhost/user/permissions state recovered
Ran a final clean publish-from-node1/consume-from-node3 round trip (5 messages) confirming app_user can publish and consume end-to-end post-recovery
Reset app_user password and stored it root-only (0600) at /root/rabbit_app_password on node1 (not disclosed in this report); verified login still succeeds via pika

evidence.summary: join_cluster succeeded for node2 and node3 against node1; cluster_status shows all 3 as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes

evidence.requirement: payments vhost and app_user account created with publish/consume permissions
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments, add_user app_user, set_permissions -p payments app_user '.*' '.*' '.*' all succeeded; list_vhosts/list_users/list_permissions confirm state

evidence.requirement: Durable quorum queue replicated across all nodes
evidence.summary: list_queues shows orders queue type=quorum with members=[rabbit@node1, rabbit@node3, rabbit@node2] and 5 messages present

evidence.requirement: Messages survive loss of node1 and remain consumable
evidence.summary: node1 rebooted (boot_id changed), queue still showed 5 messages afterward, and all 5 were consumed successfully from node2

evidence.requirement: Messages survive loss of node3 (confirmed down) and stay consumable from node2
evidence.summary: node3 stopped via rabbitmqctl stop_app; node1 cluster_status confirmed Running Nodes = [node1, node2] only (node3 absent); node2 successfully consumed all 10 pending durable messages while node3 was down

evidence.requirement: Final clean end-to-end publish/consume as app_user after full recovery
evidence.summary: 5 messages published from node1, confirmed replicated to all 3 members, consumed successfully from node3, and pika login re-verified as app_user with the final rotated password

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f captured while rabbitmq active; reboot acked; new boot_id 93ac62e9 confirmed with uptime 0; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running post-restart

evidence.requirement: Node2 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f7db4b4e captured; reboot acked; new boot_id 4313a848 confirmed with uptime 0; cluster_status from node3 later confirmed node2 rejoined as running node

evidence.requirement: Node3 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id df8bab0d captured; reboot acked; new boot_id 9ebfaa75 confirmed with uptime 0; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running post-restart

evidence.requirement: Quorum preserved throughout (never restarted/disrupted more than one node at a time)
evidence.summary: Each disruption sequence shows exactly 2 of 3 nodes remaining available throughout, and full 3/3 cluster health confirmed before proceeding to the next node
